findings.title: Recreate exit code silently renumbered from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a new meaning
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is now reused for `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The exit code of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` is explicitly documented as the stable contract for automation (see update-compatibility.adoc: "they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command"). Any script or operator logic written against the previously shipped behaviour that treats 4 as "recreate required" will now see 4 for a completely different condition (feature not enabled) and will see an undefined 3 when a recreate is actually required, so the branch selecting recreate vs. rolling can be taken wrongly or the pipeline will abort with an "unknown exit code". If this renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out as a breaking change in the release notes/migration docs, and all consumers (including the operator code that interprets the command's exit status) must be verified to use the constant rather than a literal.

findings.title: No test asserts the new/changed exit codes (3 for recreate, 4 for feature disabled)
findings.body: The PR changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 and introduces 4 for "feature disabled", yet no test verifies either value. `testFeatureNotEnabled` (line 48-50) only asserts the stderr message and never checks that the process exits with 4, and `testWrongVersions` (lines 96-106) only asserts the error message and never checks that the incompatible case exits with 3. Only the success path asserts an exit code (`assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`). Since the exit code is the documented, scriptable contract of this command, a regression in the numbering would pass CI unnoticed. Additionally, the feature-disabled path is only exercised for the `metadata` subcommand; the `check` subcommand's new guard is untested.

findings.title: CAUTION about required feature contradicts the documented default behaviour
findings.body: The new CAUTION states "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." but the same section documents `<not set>` (default) as a supported value that "Mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior", and the operator upgrade test in this PR (UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment) deliberately does NOT enable the feature for the default-strategy case and still expects normal reconciliation. As written, users will believe their existing CRs without `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` are broken. The text should state precisely when the feature is required (e.g., only when `spec.update.strategy` is set) and what "fail" means (CR rejected, status condition, pod not started).

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented only for `check` but is also returned by `metadata`, with a misleading description
findings.body: `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` now also exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) when the feature is off, but the exit-code table is placed under the "Checking the Metadata" section and describes 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." For the `metadata` command no upgrade decision is made at all, so a script reading that table will interpret a failed metadata generation as a recreate decision. The description should state that the feature is disabled and the command did not run, and the "Generating the Metadata" section should mention its possible exit codes.

findings.title: Shared macro appends the build-time option --features to a runtime command line
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now emits `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters} --features=rolling-updates` for every example in the guides. `features` is a build-time option: on an optimized/pre-built distribution (the common container case, and whenever `--optimized` is used, which this command supports via OptimizedMixin) specifying it on the command line fails instead of enabling the feature, and on a non-optimized distribution it forces a re-augmentation on every invocation. The guide should instead tell users to enable the feature at build time (`kc.sh build --features=rolling-updates` / `KC_FEATURES`) and keep the example command free of build-time options.
